hp.title: Hit Points (HP)
text: How much punishment a character can still take. Damage reduces HP, healing restores it, but never above the maximum.
At 0 HP a player character falls unconscious and starts making death saving throws.
If the damage left over after reaching 0 HP is at least the HP maximum, the character dies outright.

tempHp.title: Temporary Hit Points
text: A buffer that absorbs damage before your real HP drop. Example: 5 temporary HP and 8 damage → the 5 are gone and HP drop by 3.
They are not healing and do not stack: if you gain new ones, you choose whether to keep the old or the new. The app keeps the higher value.
Unless stated otherwise, they disappear after a long rest.

deathSaves.title: Death Saving Throws
text: A creature lying at 0 HP rolls a d20 with no bonus at the start of each of its turns.
10 or higher = success, lower = failure. 3 successes: the character is stable (unconscious, but out of danger). 3 failures: the character dies.
A 1 counts as two failures, a 20 restores 1 HP immediately.
Damage at 0 HP counts as a failure (a critical hit as two). Any healing ends the saving throws.

ac.title: Armour Class (AC)
text: How hard a character is to hit. An attack hits if the attack roll equals or exceeds the target's AC.
In this app, players never see the AC of enemies.

spellSlots.title: Spell Slots
text: Spellcasters have a number of slots per spell level (I to IX). Casting a spell of level I or higher uses a slot of that level or higher.
Cantrips (level 0) need no slot.
Expended slots return after a long rest. Warlocks regain theirs after a short rest.
In the app: tap a diamond = expended (grey). Characters without spells can hide this section under “Customise sheet”.

counters.title: Counters
text: For anything with limited uses: ki points, rage, potions of healing, inspiration and so on.
“−” and “+” count down and up. “Customise sheet” has ready-made presets you can add or leave out.

initiative.title: Initiative
text: Determines the order at the start of a combat: everyone rolls d20 + Dexterity modifier. The highest goes first.
Identical enemies often roll together and act as a group.
In the app: type in the values, “Sort”, then “Next ▶” to move on.

advantage.title: Advantage and Disadvantage
text: Advantage: roll two d20s and use the higher. Disadvantage: roll two d20s and use the lower.
If you have both at once, they cancel out: roll normally.
The dice window has “Advantage” and “Disadvantage” buttons for this.

coins.title: Coins
text: 1 platinum piece (pp) = 10 gold pieces (gp). 1 gp = 10 silver pieces (sp). 1 sp = 10 copper pieces (cp).
50 coins weigh about 1 pound.

visibility.title: Visibility in the portrait bar
text: Automatic: the enemy only appears for a player once that player can see at least one of its tokens on the map. A hidden ambush does not give itself away.
Always show: the entry is always visible to everyone, even without a token on the map (e.g. a voice from the dark).
Hide: the entry is never visible to players, only to you.

abilities.title: Ability Scores and Modifiers
text: Every character has six abilities: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma. A score of 10–11 is average.
Each score gives a modifier: (score − 10) ÷ 2, rounded down. 8–9 gives −1, 12–13 gives +2, 16–17 gives +3, 20 gives +5.
The modifier applies to almost every roll with that ability: ability checks, skills, saving throws, attacks.
The app calculates the modifier automatically.

proficiency.title: Proficiency Bonus
text: A bonus for everything the character is proficient in: certain skills, saving throws, weapons, tools and spell attacks.
It depends only on level: level 1–4 +2, 5–8 +3, 9–12 +4, 13–16 +5, 17–20 +6.
It is added at most once per roll (doubled for expertise).

skills.title: Skills, Proficiency and Expertise
text: Each skill belongs to an ability, e.g. Stealth to Dexterity. Bonus = that ability's modifier.
First dot (P) = proficient: add the proficiency bonus.
Second dot (E) = expertise (e.g. rogue, bard): add the proficiency bonus twice.
The dots can only be changed after “✎ Edit”, so nothing flips by accident.

saves.title: Saving Throws
text: A saving throw resists a danger, e.g. poison (Constitution) or a fireball (Dexterity).
Roll: d20 + the ability modifier, plus the proficiency bonus if the character is proficient in that saving throw (usually two from the class).
If the result equals or exceeds the difficulty class (DC), the save succeeds.

passivePerception.title: Passive Perception
text: How alert a character is without actively searching. Score: 10 + Perception bonus.
The DM compares it, for example, with the Stealth check of a lurking enemy. Advantage gives +5, disadvantage −5.

level.title: Level
text: The character's experience level (1–20). It determines the proficiency bonus.
Entered by the player.

alignment.title: Alignment
text: A rough moral outlook in two parts: lawful – neutral – chaotic (order) and good – neutral – evil (morality).
Examples: lawful good (helps others, follows the rules), chaotic neutral (follows their whims).
It describes the character; it does not force them to do anything.

size.title: Size
text: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan. Most races are Medium; halflings and gnomes are Small.
On the map a Medium creature occupies one square (5 × 5 ft), a Large one 2 × 2 squares, a Huge one 3 × 3.

attackBonus.title: Attack Bonus
text: What is added to the d20 for an attack roll. It hits if the total equals or exceeds the target's AC.
Melee weapon: Strength modifier + proficiency bonus (if proficient). Ranged weapon: Dexterity + proficiency bonus. Finesse weapons may use Dexterity.
Spell attack: spellcasting ability modifier (e.g. Intelligence for a wizard) + proficiency bonus.
Damage: the weapon's dice + the same ability modifier (without proficiency bonus).

effects.title: Effect timers
text: Keeps track of how many rounds an effect has left, e.g. Bless (up to 10 rounds = 1 minute) or a net.
With every new round of combat the timer counts down by one. At 0 it turns red: the effect is over.
1 round lasts about 6 seconds; 1 minute is 10 rounds.

round.title: Round
text: In a round every combatant takes one turn (about 6 seconds of game time).
The app counts automatically: pressing “Next ▶” after the last combatant starts the next round. The DM can change the number with − and +.

units.title: Feet and metres
text: The rules use feet (ft). 1 foot = 0.3048 m.
German rulebooks round: 5 ft (one square) = 1.5 m, 30 ft = 9 m.

blinded: Can't see and automatically fails any check that requires sight.
Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
charmed: Can't attack the charmer or target them with harmful abilities or spells.
The charmer has advantage on social checks against the creature.
deafened: Can't hear and automatically fails any check that requires hearing.
frightened: Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is in sight.
Can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.
grappled: Speed becomes 0 and can't benefit from any bonus to speed.
Ends if the grappler is incapacitated or the creature is moved out of the grappler's reach.
invisible: Impossible to see without magic or a special sense; heavily obscured for the purpose of hiding. Noise or tracks can give it away.
Attack rolls against the creature have disadvantage; its own attack rolls have advantage.
paralyzed: Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Attack rolls against it have advantage. Any hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit.
petrified: Transformed, with any non-magical equipment, into stone (or another solid substance): weight increases tenfold, it stops ageing.
Incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of its surroundings.
Attack rolls against it have advantage; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Resistance to all damage, immune to poison and disease (existing ones are only suspended).
poisoned: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
prone: Can only crawl until it stands up (costs half its movement), which ends the condition.
Disadvantage on its own attack rolls.
Attack rolls from within 5 ft have advantage; from further away, disadvantage.
restrained: Speed becomes 0 and can't benefit from any bonus to speed.
Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
stunned: Incapacitated, can't move and can speak only falteringly.
Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Attack rolls against it have advantage.
unconscious: Incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of its surroundings.
Drops whatever it is holding and falls prone.
Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Attack rolls against it have advantage. Any hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit.
exhaustion: Has 6 levels whose effects add up: 1 disadvantage on ability checks · 2 speed halved · 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws · 4 HP maximum halved · 5 speed 0 · 6 death.
A long rest with food and drink reduces the level by 1. Track the level as a counter.
surprised: A creature surprised at the start of combat can't move or take an action on its first turn.
It also can't take reactions until that turn ends.
blessed: Bless spell: up to three creatures add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws.
Lasts up to 1 minute while the caster concentrates.
concentration: Some spells only last while you concentrate. You can concentrate on only one such spell at a time.
When you take damage: Constitution saving throw, DC 10 or half the damage (whichever is higher). On a failure the spell ends. Being incapacitated or killed also ends it.
slowed: Slow spell: speed halved, −2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws, no reactions.
On its turn only an action or a bonus action, and at most one attack.
At the end of each of its turns it may make a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect.
burning: Not an official condition. How much fire damage it takes each turn and how the fire is put out is up to the DM (often: an action to put it out).
bleeding: Not an official condition. How much damage it takes each turn and what stops the bleeding (e.g. healing or a Medicine check) is up to the DM.
